title: 1951 AHSME Problem 30
statement: If two poles \(20''\) and \(80''\) high are \(100''\) apart, then the height of the intersection of the lines joining the top of each pole to the foot of the opposite pole is:

solutions.text:
Put the bases at \((0,0)\) and \((100,0),\) with tops \((0,80)\) and \((100,20).\) The cross-lines are \(y=\frac45x\) and \(y=20-\frac15x.\) Equating them gives \(x=20,\) and hence \(y=16.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Place the pole bases at \(x=0\) and \(x=100\)
The cross-lines can be written \(y=\frac{4x}{5}\) and \(y=20-\frac{x}{5}\)
